title: Handley Page Halifax BB320
memorial_details: Rectangular brass plaque screwed onto a stone backplate and mounted on the wall of the Blakley Lane Methodist Chapel. Dedication is incised in black, lower-case script.
inscription: NEAR THIS SPOT ON 7TH FEBRUARY 1944/ PERISHED THE CREW OF HANDLEY PAGE HALIFAX BB320/ Fg Off Hubert Lloyd Kerr RCAF/ Fg Off Ernest Charles David Richards RAFVR/ Sgt Kenneth Murray RAFVR/ Sgt William Desmond Joshua RAFVR/ [and two comrades]/ ROYAL AIR FORCE VOLUNTEER RESERVE AND/ (name)/ ROYAL CANADIAN AIR FORCE/ "PER ARDUA AD ASTRA" - WWW.INTERNATIONALBCC.CO.UK/ PLAQUE UNVEILED 7TH FEBRUARY 2020
narrative: It emerged from cloud spinning and crashed near Cheadle, Staffordshire, on 7 February 1944. All six crew died. The crew were Flying Officer Ernest Richards (pilot, 26), Flying Officer Hubert Kerr of the RCAF (air bomber, 28), Sergeant Kenneth Murray (navigator, 23), Sergeant Albert Denny (flight engineer, 28), Sergeant William Joshua (wireless operator/air gunner, 22) and Sergeant Herbert Couling (air gunner, 20). They were buried at Chester (Blacon) Cemetery (Richards, Kerr and Couling), Darlington West Cemetery (Murray), Sarn Cemetery (Joshua) and Streatham Cemetery (Denny).

crew.name: Kenneth Murray
crew.burial_location: Darlington West Cemetery, Section V.7E, Grave 301

key_details: Training flight crashed about 6.30pm on 7 Feb 1944 on farmland about 200 yards from the A52, beside the chapel near Kingsley Moor
Local historian Martyn Hordern rediscovered the story
Plaque funded by Kingsley Parish Council; RAF, parish councillors, Royal British Legion and residents attended the unveiling

community_connection: A brass plaque on the wall of Blakeley Lane Methodist Chapel names the crew. It was unveiled on 7 February 2020. The Leek Post & Times reported that Kingsley Parish Council funded it, and that the story was rediscovered by local historian Martyn Hordern.
cause_of_loss: Emerged from cloud spinning, and crashed near Cheadle, Staffordshire
memorial_address: Blakeley Lane Methodist Chapel, junction of Blakeley Lane and Cheadle Road (A52), ST10 2PS
